title: Crystal Structure Based Graph Neural Network And LLM Multi-Modal Approach for Material Magnetic Ordering Prediction
authors: Adam Zheng, April Zheng, Sheng Ran
abstract: AI/ML models are useful for the prediction of materials' properties. Recently, there has been great progress in developing Neural Network models to predict the properties of solids, molecules, and crystals, avoiding expensive and time-consuming laboratory testing. This study presents a novel AI/ML-based multi-modal approach to predict material magnetic ordering using material crystal structure information as input to a Graph Neural Network model (GNN) and semantic text descriptions of the material's properties and structure as input to a Large Language Model (LLM), before performing information fusion of the GNN and LLM outputs to predict material magnetic ordering in four classes (Non-magnetic, Ferromagnetic, Antiferromagnetic, Ferrimagnetic). The model is trained, validated, and tested on a dataset which is a combination of Materials Project dataset, Magndata dataset, and a set of uranium compounds with magnetic ordering determined in laboratory testing, with an 80/10/10 (training/validation/testing) data split. The proposed GNN and LLM multi-modal approach achieves better overall accuracy than both the standalone GNN and LLM approaches with three fusion strategies.

infographic.key_insight: Combining crystal-structure GNN outputs with an LLM text branch improves overall accuracy for predicting four magnetic-ordering classes over either standalone model.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could support computational screening of magnetic materials before costly laboratory characterization.
method: Encode crystal structures with a graph neural network.
Process semantic descriptions of material properties and structure with an LLM.
Fuse outputs using three strategies to classify non-magnetic, ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, or ferrimagnetic ordering.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation uses combined Materials Project, Magndata, and experimentally characterized uranium-compound data with an 80/10/10 training/validation/test split; the abstract reports improved overall accuracy but no numerical scores.
infographic.watch_item: Text descriptions should be checked for magnetic-label leakage to ensure gains reflect predictive information rather than disclosed answers.
infographic.paper_title: Crystal Structure Based Graph Neural Network And LLM Multi-Modal Approach for Material Magnetic Ordering Prediction

title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
authors: Joseph Hart, Samuel G. H. Brookes, Fabian L. Thiemann, Christoph Schran
abstract: Foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise broad transferability, yet their out-of-domain reliability is hard to establish. Here, we use pure and O/H-containing disordered carbon spanning multiple phases, competing hybridisations and porous frameworks to stress-test six popular foundation MLIPs. We first screen all six on density functional theory (DFT) energy and force errors and binding curves, then subject four to melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics and evaluate the resulting structural observables. Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories reveal unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures that low DFT energy and force errors fail to reveal. Of the models tested, MACE-MH-1 is the most consistently robust, with low DFT errors and stable MD. Despite differing architectures, OMAT-based models share structural biases, highlighting the importance of training coverage. All four models generate structures of nanoporous carbon that reproduce the principal experimental and specialised carbon potential signatures. Incorporating O/H leaves short-range order largely unchanged but shifts pore-size distributions towards larger pores. These results emphasise the need for application-specific validation and extend molecular dynamics modelling of nanoporous carbon towards experimentally realistic structures.

infographic.key_insight: Low DFT energy and force errors do not guarantee reliable disordered-carbon simulations; MACE-MH-1 was the most consistently robust foundation model tested.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Foundation potentials can support nanoporous-carbon modelling, but application-specific stability and structural validation are essential before deployment.
method: Screen six foundation MLIPs using DFT energy and force errors and binding curves.
Run melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics with four models.
Evaluate structural observables in pure and O/H-containing disordered carbons.
infographic.evidence_signal: Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories exposed failures missed by error metrics, while all four MD-tested models reproduced principal experimental and specialised-potential signatures of nanoporous carbon.
infographic.watch_item: Shared structural biases among OMAT-based models suggest that training coverage can limit reliability despite architectural differences.
infographic.paper_title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons

title: Instability-driven segregation of V group transition metals on HEB$_2$ grain boundaries influencing enhanced mechanical properties
authors: Daniil Alekseev, Viktor S. Baidyshev, Alexander G. Kvashnin
abstract: Five metals share a common sublattice in the (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B$_2$ (HEB$_2$). Most high-entropy materials are produced as polycrystalline materials in the form of sintered ceramics. The question of which metal species are located at grain boundaries is still unknown. Here, we calculated the grain-boundary energy $γ_{GB}$ of four types of boundaries in five binary diborides and HEB$_2$ using density functional theory (DFT). We analyzed the bonding at these boundaries using COHP and sampled cation segregation at six boundaries of HEB$_2$, ordered and general, using Monte Carlo / molecular dynamics with a MACE potential that was fine-tuned for this system. According to our results $γ_{GB}$ splits by group: the group V diborides NbB$_2$ and TaB$_2$ form boundaries with about half the energy of the group IV at three of the four types of GBs, ranging from 0.8 to 2.7 compared to 2.5--4.8~J/m$^2$. COHP shows a significant difference at the Fermi level, namely the Me--B bonds of NbB$_2$ and TaB$_2$ are antibonding at Fermi energy ($E_F$) in the bulk but bonding at the GB, while their integrated strength hardly changes. In HEB$_2$ the segregation follows a similar pattern: Nb and Ta are enriched at five of the six grain boundaries, including general boundaries, up to 23--35~at.\% at 2000~K, although the size of the atoms would favor Zr and Hf in the expanded sites. A segregated $Σ193$ grain boundary can withstand 26 against 20~GPa for a random boundary in tension at 300~K. The grain boundaries of HEB$_2$ are composed of group V metals, as suggested by the boundary energies of binaries compounds and their bonding at the Fermi level. Grain boundaries of the (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B$_2$ preferentially include Nb and Ta. This lowers the grain boundary energy and strengthens the boundaries. This consists of the lower boundary energy and changes Fermi level bonding in NbB$_2$ and TaB$_2$.

infographic.key_insight: Nb and Ta preferentially segregate to grain boundaries in (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B₂, linking favorable boundary bonding and lower boundary energies to stronger interfaces.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling grain-boundary chemistry could improve the mechanical performance of high-entropy diboride ceramics.
method: DFT calculations of four grain-boundary types in five binary diborides and HEB₂.
COHP analysis of metal–boron bonding near the Fermi level.
Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics segregation sampling at six HEB₂ boundaries using a fine-tuned MACE potential.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nb and Ta were enriched at five of six simulated boundaries, reaching 23–35 at.% at 2000 K; a segregated Σ193 boundary sustained 26 GPa versus 20 GPa for a random boundary in tension at 300 K.
infographic.watch_item: The computational findings require experimental validation, and the reported tensile-strength gain is specific to the tested Σ193 boundary.
infographic.paper_title: Instability-driven segregation of V group transition metals on HEB$_2$ grain boundaries influencing enhanced mechanical properties

title: Design and synthesis of laser inscribed flexible Bragg gratings containing silicon oxynitride-doped silicon thin film for authentication applications with the insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Quantum Mechanical Calculations
authors: Ali Karatutlu, Timuçin Emre Tabaru, Umut Taylan, Zehra Gizem Mutlay, Doğukan Hazar Özbey, Okan Uslu
abstract: Silicon-on-insulator is mostly the main driving material system for the field of silicon photonics, including PICs, due to high index contrast and compatibility with current semiconductor manufacturing processes [1]. A recent example is silicon oxynitride-doped silicon [2] discovered recently by our group, offering to set a new position for the fields of silicon photonics with a precise control of refractive index from 2.1 to 2.5 together with the photosensitivity property at different wavelengths. In this study, we demonstrate that the synthesis of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon can be performed on a flexible substrate for the fabrication of Bragg gratings (BG) at low temperatures below 100 degrees Celsius that are emerging for advanced applications. Their use in preserving ultra-fast lasers inscribed micro-information has been demonstrated numerically and experimentally due to its multispectral reflection behaviour from the ultraviolet (UV) to the near-infrared (NIR) regions. The unique structural characteristics of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon were studied at the Si L, O K and N K edges using soft X-ray absorption studies. The quantum mechanical calculations provide the potential formation mechanism of SiON-doped Si, whereas the crystal structure prediction for bulk Si3N4-xOx was conducted using the particle swarm optimization method in combination with density functional theory (DFT).

infographic.key_insight: Silicon oxynitride-doped silicon enables laser-inscribed flexible Bragg gratings with UV-to-NIR reflection for authentication applications.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Fabrication below 100 °C and refractive-index control from 2.1 to 2.5 offer a route to flexible photonic structures that preserve laser-written micro-information.
method: Synthesize silicon oxynitride-doped silicon on flexible substrates and inscribe Bragg gratings using ultrafast lasers.
Probe local structure with soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Si L, O K and N K edges.
Investigate formation mechanisms with quantum calculations and predict bulk Si3N4−xOx structures using particle swarm optimization coupled with DFT.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical and experimental demonstrations of micro-information preservation through multispectral reflection, but provides no quantitative performance metrics.
infographic.watch_item: Durability under repeated bending and authentication reliability remain unquantified in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Design and synthesis of laser inscribed flexible Bragg gratings containing silicon oxynitride-doped silicon thin film for authentication applications with the insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Quantum Mechanical Calculations

title: Stabilization of Ferroelectric Domains via Interfacial Strain in HoFeO3- BaTiO3 Nanofiber Heterostructures for Enhanced Hybrid Energy Harvesting
authors: Smita Chaturvedi, Swathi Krishna, Shivshankar Jokare, Supriya Sahoo, Vikash Kushwaha, Priyank Shyam
abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are an attractive platform for self-powered mechanical-energy harvesting, but their output is often limited by depolarization fields, charge leakage, and inefficient stress transfer to the active dipoles, particularly in polymer-dominated composites. Here we report HoFeO3-BaTiO3 (HFO-BTO) nanofiber heterostructures prepared by alternating sol-gel electrospinning, in which orthorhombic HoFeO3 (Pbnm) and tetragonal BaTiO3 (P4mm) coexist in intimate contact. Rietveld-refined X-ray diffraction, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy indicate interfacial lattice distortion. Polarization-electric field loops show that the heterostructure retains a polarization comparable to that of BaTiO3 (16.39 vs 15.80 microcoulombs per square centimeter at zero field) while its switching-current maximum moves to a higher field (about 7 vs about 3.5 kilovolts per centimeter), consistent with strain-stabilized ferroelectric domains. When the nanofibers are encapsulated in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and excited under cyclic impact, the device produces a hybrid output: the piezoelectric response of the strained BaTiO3 is supplemented by a triboelectric contribution from contact electrification. The HFO-BTO device delivers open-circuit voltage peaks of about +6 volts and -8 volts and a power density of 24.31 microwatts per cubic centimeter at a 4.7 megaohm load. This is 2.4 times the value for an identically fabricated BaTiO3 device (10.00 microwatts per cubic centimeter) and 8.7 times that of the HoFeO3 device (2.78 microwatts per cubic centimeter). These results link interface-driven lattice distortion to improved electromechanical output and identify all-oxide nanofiber heterostructures as a promising route to lead-free energy harvesting.

infographic.key_insight: Interfacial lattice distortion in HoFeO3–BaTiO3 nanofibers is consistent with stabilized ferroelectric domains and enhanced hybrid mechanical-energy harvesting.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Lead-free oxide heterostructures offer a route to improve energy-harvester output through interface engineering rather than polymer-dominated designs.
method: Fabricate HoFeO3–BaTiO3 heterostructures by alternating sol–gel electrospinning.
Probe lattice distortion and polarization using XRD refinement, HRTEM, Raman spectroscopy, and electrical measurements.
Encapsulate nanofibers in PDMS and evaluate hybrid piezoelectric–triboelectric output under cyclic impact.
infographic.evidence_signal: The heterostructure delivered 24.31 µW/cm³ at a 4.7 MΩ load—2.4× the BaTiO3 control and 8.7× the HoFeO3 control—with open-circuit peaks near +6 V and −8 V.
infographic.watch_item: The hybrid output does not isolate the piezoelectric and triboelectric contributions, limiting attribution of the gain solely to strain-stabilized domains.
infographic.paper_title: Stabilization of Ferroelectric Domains via Interfacial Strain in HoFeO3- BaTiO3 Nanofiber Heterostructures for Enhanced Hybrid Energy Harvesting

title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
authors: Reza T Batley, Sourav Saha
abstract: Bone scaffolds must reconcile a macroscale mechanical response with microscale geometric feasibility, yet conventional approaches to their design restrict attainable constitutive properties. This work presents a concurrent two-scale topology optimization framework; a conditional rectified flow generates periodic lattice microstructures, which are then refined in latent space by exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities. The resulting unit-cell geometries and their spatial assignments are jointly optimized under mechanical and feature-size constraints. In a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all eight flow-started refinements produce printable cells with maximum relative errors under 1\% across six prescribed engineering moduli. Constructing the implant from a single tiled cell reproduces intact whole-femur compliance within 0.1\% and regional strain energy within 0.35\% under four loading conditions. In human femoral reconstruction, multiscale concurrent optimization produces a cortical mid-shaft scaffold with porosity 63\% while satisfying the compliance constraint within 2\% under walking and stair-climbing loads. It achieves an 84\% porosity on a proximal cancellous scaffold with strain-energy deviations below 0.25\% under the same loads. Analysis of the learned representations reveals distinct architectural families in latent space. Further, the attention heads of the rectified-flow transformer specialize for spatial shifts -- learning the analogue of a finite-difference stencil -- and coordinate symmetries, with ablations showing their influence on generated topologies. These results establish a route to printable, mechanically constrained scaffold designs. The framework is general enough for extending to many other multiscale structural design applications including topology-microstructure co-design in metal additive manufacturing.

infographic.key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent optimization of printable bone-scaffold microstructures and their spatial placement to meet mechanical targets.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework supports highly porous, mechanically constrained implants and could extend to topology–microstructure co-design for metal additive manufacturing.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells using a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometry and spatial assignment under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
infographic.evidence_signal: All eight rabbit-benchmark refinements achieved under 1% maximum relative error across six target moduli; human femur designs reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance within 2% and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports computational benchmarks; physical print fidelity, fatigue durability, and biological performance remain to be validated.
infographic.paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement

title: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories
authors: Yuki K. Wakabayashi, Yui Ogawa
abstract: Self-driving laboratories accelerate materials exploration through autonomous closed-loop integration of synthesis, characterization, and next-experiment selection. However, characterization does not always directly provide the target property; measured spectra or images often require automated analysis to extract quantitative descriptors based on physically motivated assumptions and predefined criteria. Such procedures can fail for measurements outside these criteria, requiring a decision on whether a reliable value can be recovered or no numerical value should be reported. Here, we implemented an autonomous adaptive spectral-analysis agent using a large language model (LLM) to supervise a deterministic numerical-analysis routine. For each spectrum, the agent executes the predefined analysis script and assesses the result using the measured spectrum and fitting diagnostics. Valid results are accepted unchanged, recoverable failures are reanalyzed through bounded adjustments of predefined fitting parameters, and NaN (not a number) is returned when no scientifically defensible value can be obtained. We evaluated the workflow on optical transmittance spectra from 203 epitaxial beta-Ga2O3 films grown during a previously reported self-driving thin-film growth campaign. The predefined optical analysis script returned Urbach energy, an optical-quality metric, for 183 spectra and failed for 20. The agent retained those 183 values and evaluated 20 exception cases, recovering 16 through bounded parameter adjustments and returning NaN for 4 when the spectral evidence did not support a reliable Urbach tail. The audit records captured spectral features, parameter changes, and rationale for each decision. These results demonstrate autonomous scientific exception handling by an LLM agent while leaving quantitative property extraction to deterministic numerical analysis.

infographic.key_insight: An LLM agent recovered usable Urbach-energy estimates from failed spectral analyses while leaving numerical extraction to deterministic code.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Autonomous exception handling can reduce manual analysis bottlenecks in self-driving laboratories without forcing unreliable property estimates.
method: Run a predefined deterministic spectral-analysis script.
Assess spectra and fitting diagnostics; retain valid results unchanged.
Retry failures with bounded fitting-parameter adjustments, returning NaN when evidence is insufficient.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 203 β-Ga2O3 film spectra, the agent retained 183 baseline estimates, recovered 16 of 20 failures, and returned NaN for 4.
infographic.watch_item: Evaluation covered one material and measurement workflow; reliability across other spectra and fitting models remains unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories

title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
authors: Ilya V. Chepkasov, Alexander V. Shapeev, Alexander G. Kvashnin
abstract: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.

infographic.key_insight: Active learning improves data efficiency by selecting reference calculations that adapt machine-learning interatomic potentials to their intended simulation conditions.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This approach can focus expensive reference calculations on configurations relevant to materials mechanics, diffusion, functional behavior, and reactive dynamics.
method: Iterate candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating.
Compare uncertainty-, kernel-, and representation-based acquisition strategies.
Review on-the-fly training, pretrained-model adaptation, and reaction-aware sampling.
infographic.evidence_signal: The review surveys more than 70 studies, emphasizing 2020–2026, but the abstract reports no pooled quantitative performance benchmark.
infographic.watch_item: Uncertainty estimates are architecture-dependent and may be least reliable in the unfamiliar configurations where accurate acquisition matters most.
infographic.paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency

title: Atomic-level study of dose-dependent lattice thermal conductivity degradation in irradiated tungsten
authors: Mary K Chessey, José Julio Gutiérrez Moreno, Sajjan Singh Mehta, Paolo Settembri, Arda Erbasan, Dominik Freinberger
abstract: Plasma-facing components (PFCs) in future fusion reactors must withstand extreme environments, making tungsten (W) a prime candidate material due to its high thermal conductivity, high melting temperature, low sputtering yield, low tritium absorption. However, neutron irradiation introduces complex nanostructural defects that severely degrade these critical properties. In this work, we use Non-Equilibrium Molecular Dynamics (NEMD) simulations coupled with the Creation Relaxation Algorithm (CRA) to investigate the lattice thermal conductivity (kappa) of W across a wide range of irradiation doses. Systems treated with different doses up to 1.8 canonical displacements per atom (cdpa) were simulated to generate and study diverse defect structures, including vacancies and self-interstitial atom (SIA) clusters. By correlating spatially-resolved temperature gradients with local defect concentrations, we show that even small changes in defect type and distribution significantly affect thermal transport. We employ Machine Learning (ML) models to develop a quantitative relationship between the defect features and the resulting thermal conductivity degradation. The ML analysis identifies vacancy density as the dominant structural factor controlling thermal transport. We found a significant, nonlinear suppression of kappa with increasing defect density. Predictive multi-defect mapping built upon our ML model resolved a step-like degradation transition at a critical vacancy threshold of 0.05 at.%, beyond which phonon scattering completely saturated and capped the maximum relative lattice thermal conductivity degradation at approximately 30 at.%. This integrated simulation and ML approach provides a powerful, predictive framework for quantifying the complex relationship between structure and thermal conductivity in irradiated fusion materials.

infographic.key_insight: Simulations and machine learning identify vacancy density as the dominant driver of lattice thermal conductivity loss in irradiated tungsten, with a step-like transition near 0.05 at.% vacancies.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Defect-informed thermal transport predictions could improve assessments of tungsten plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
method: Generate irradiation defects using the Creation Relaxation Algorithm at doses up to 1.8 canonical displacements per atom.
Calculate lattice thermal conductivity using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics and correlate local temperature gradients with defect concentrations.
Train machine learning models to map multiple defect features to conductivity degradation.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across simulated doses, the analysis found nonlinear conductivity suppression and a reported saturation at approximately 30% relative lattice conductivity loss.
infographic.watch_item: The study addresses simulated lattice heat transport; experimental validation and electronic heat transport remain important for predicting total tungsten thermal conductivity.
infographic.paper_title: Atomic-level study of dose-dependent lattice thermal conductivity degradation in irradiated tungsten

title: SIESTA-QCOMP: Bridging Classical and Quantum Computing for Strongly Correlated Systems
authors: Yann Pouillon, Federico Marchesin, Ivano Tavernelli, Emilio Artacho
abstract: Density Functional Theory (DFT) is the established workhorse of computational materials science, yet it faces fundamental challenges with strongly correlated electrons, such as in transition metal complexes and bond-breaking processes. While quantum computing offers a theoretically exact path to resolve these problems, current hardware limitations prohibit fully quantum simulations of realistic material systems. To bridge this gap, we present SIESTA-QCOMP, a modular suite embedding quantum methodologies within DFT. Harnessing SIESTA's localised basis set, we implement a projection-based embedding scheme that treats the bulk environment classically while mapping the strongly correlated "impurity" subspace to a quantum processor. The architecture uses a socket-based driver to orchestrate workflows between the Fortran-based SIESTA engine and Python-based frameworks like Qiskit, ensuring high interoperability. We detail the hybrid workflow, currently utilising a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and discuss the road map toward methods such as Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD). We illustrate the framework on an hypothetical iron porphyrin calculation and argue that such hybrid architectures are not merely interim solutions but essential foundations for integrating quantum utility into materials design, as envisioned by our broader QCOMP4DFT initiative.

infographic.key_insight: SIESTA-QCOMP combines classical DFT with quantum treatment of strongly correlated subspaces to target materials problems beyond standard DFT.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Its modular architecture connects SIESTA with quantum software frameworks, providing a route toward hybrid materials simulations under quantum hardware constraints.
method: Use SIESTA’s localised basis for projection-based embedding.
Treat the environment classically and map the correlated impurity subspace to a quantum processor.
Coordinate Fortran SIESTA and Python frameworks such as Qiskit through a socket-based driver, currently using VQE.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract describes a hypothetical iron porphyrin illustration but reports no quantitative accuracy, scaling, or hardware benchmarks.
infographic.watch_item: Practical accuracy and computational benefit remain unestablished; current hardware limits feasible quantum subspaces, and SQD is a roadmap method.
infographic.paper_title: SIESTA-QCOMP: Bridging Classical and Quantum Computing for Strongly Correlated Systems

title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books
authors: Skander Lejmi
abstract: A market maker provides liquidity by quoting prices to buy and sell an asset, earning the spread while managing inventory risk. We study market makers trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning on prediction markets, specifically Polymarket, whose thin order books pose distinct challenges. Three challenges underpin this research: adverse selection may cause a policy trained on real data to stop quoting; the consequences of a quote can arrive many steps after the action; and prediction-market L2 data does not identify individual orders needed for simulation. We address these challenges by reconstructing order-level LOBSTER-format data from Polymarket and training agents in JaxMARL-HFT on 417 real markets. We enrich the baseline market maker's observation space with the book and recent flow, redesign its actions and inventory controls, and propose a cooperative multi-agent decomposition into a quoter and a risk manager trained using recurrent Independent Proximal Policy Optimisation (IPPO) with RNN policies. We investigate reward shaping, particularly reward blending and post-fill markout, to mitigate credit-assignment difficulties between the agents. Our redesigned single-agent market maker quotes more frequently and incurs smaller held-out losses than the retrained JaxMARL-HFT baseline, although the contributions of jointly changed observations, actions and risk constraints are not separately identified. Decomposition alone performs poorly; careful reward design substantially improves the desk relative to the unshaped split and yields our best result. Models are evaluated on realised end-of-episode portfolio value on held-out markets. None establishes positive average portfolio value in periodic held-out evaluation, and each configuration was trained with one seed. The environment, data and protocol lay a foundation for makers that quote many linked markets at once.

infographic.key_insight: Cooperative quoter and risk-manager agents achieve the strongest reported market-making result only with careful reward shaping, not decomposition alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework supports liquidity-provision research for thin prediction-market order books by combining reconstructed order data with inventory-aware reinforcement learning.
method: Reconstruct order-level LOBSTER-format data from Polymarket L2 feeds.
Redesign market-maker observations, actions and inventory controls in JaxMARL-HFT.
Train recurrent IPPO quoter and risk-manager agents with reward blending and post-fill markout.
infographic.evidence_signal: Training used 417 real markets, with evaluation based on realised end-of-episode portfolio value on held-out markets; no configuration established positive average portfolio value.
infographic.watch_item: Each configuration used one training seed, and jointly changed observations, actions and risk constraints prevent isolating their individual contributions.
infographic.paper_title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Discovery of Carbon-Related Defect Formation Mechanisms in Diamond
authors: Grace Huang, Christopher Fivecoat, Xun Xu, Mengen Wang
abstract: Diamond is an important host material for functional defects such as solid-state spin qubits. During the defect creation by irradiation and subsequent thermal annealing, carbon-related defects, including vacancies and interstitials, are generated and can migrate to form new defect complexes. To investigate this kinetically driven process and reveal the formation mechanisms of the di-interstitials and di-vacancies in the neutral charge state, we fine-tuned a universal machine learning interatomic potential using a small dataset generated from density functional theory calculations. We obtained a barrier of 1.84 eV for mono-interstitial migration and found that two initially separated mono-interstitials only need to overcome a lower barrier to form di-interstitial configurations. Beyond the training data, the MLIP also identified the formation pathway for an additional di-interstitial configuration and a stepwise divacancy dissociation mechanism. These results reveal migration-assisted defect complex formation mechanisms and demonstrate how targeted MLIP training can identify reaction pathways.

infographic.key_insight: A fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potential revealed migration-assisted formation pathways for carbon defect complexes in diamond.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Understanding defect migration and clustering could help guide irradiation and annealing strategies for diamond-based spin-qubit materials.
method: Generate a small training dataset using density functional theory.
Fine-tune a universal machine learning interatomic potential.
Investigate neutral interstitial and vacancy reaction pathways.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model yielded a 1.84 eV mono-interstitial migration barrier, lower barriers for pairing initially separated interstitials, and pathways beyond the training data for an additional di-interstitial configuration and stepwise divacancy dissociation.
infographic.watch_item: The study addresses neutral defects; applicability to charged defects and broader processing conditions requires further validation.
infographic.paper_title: Machine Learning-Assisted Discovery of Carbon-Related Defect Formation Mechanisms in Diamond

title: Electronic structure, magnetic order and anisotropic magnetoresistance in $\mathbf{Eu_{1-x}Gd_xCd_2P_2}$ (0 $\le$ x $\le$1)
authors: Yogendra Singh Negi, Tulika Maitra
abstract: Recently, $\text{EuCd}_2\text{P}_2$ has attracted increased attention for its colossal magnetoresistive (CMR) property, the mechanism of which seems to deviate from that of known canonical CMR compounds such as manganites. Many studies underscore the role of low density of hole carriers caused by Eu vacancies, particularly in stabilizing ferromagnetic (FM) order and modifying electrical transport and magnetoresistive responses in this compound. A magnetic polaron based mechanism rather than double exchange based mechanism is being proposed to explain the CMR effect for this compound. In this work, we explore the effect of elctron doping on the magnetic transition and CMR behaviour via Gd substitution at Eu sites with varying concentration (x) in Eu$_{1-x}$Gd$_{x}$Cd$_2$P$_2$. Our Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo-based calculations reveal an oscillating ground state magnetic order as a function of electron carrier density. The ground state is found to be A-AFM metal for x=0.056, 0.125 and 0.5 while it becomes ferromagnetic metal at x= 0.33, 0.67 and 1. Most importantly, we predict colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance in this compound for x=0.125 and 0.5. The underlying mechanism of anisotropic CMR in this compound looks similar to double exchange like due to the presence of a strong intra-site 4\textit{f}-5\textit{d} ferromagnetic exchange interaction and an itinerant electron in the hybridized conduction states. The oscillating ground state magnetic order and the enhancement of transition temperature (as high as 150K for x=0.67) as a function of electron carrier density offers a new avenue to tune the magnetotransport property in this compound and offers an excellent platform for designing future spintronics devices.

infographic.key_insight: Gd electron doping is predicted to switch Eu₁₋ₓGdₓCd₂P₂ between A-type antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic metallic states, with colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance at x = 0.125 and 0.5.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Composition-controlled magnetic order and transport could enable tunable spintronic materials, with a predicted magnetic transition temperature reaching 150 K at x = 0.67.
method: Density functional theory calculations across Gd substitution levels
Monte Carlo calculations of magnetic behavior
Analysis of intra-site 4f–5d exchange and hybridized conduction states
infographic.evidence_signal: Calculations predict A-type antiferromagnetic metals at x = 0.056, 0.125 and 0.5, and ferromagnetic metals at x = 0.33, 0.67 and 1.
infographic.watch_item: The predicted colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance requires experimental validation; the abstract reports no measured magnitude or room-temperature operation.

title: Tunable annealing of defects in self-aligning active crystals
authors: Kanka Ghosh, Andreas M. Menzel
abstract: Obtaining defect-free single-crystals is of crucial importance in soft matter and materials science, spanning both fundamental interests and practical applications. Active crystals, encompassing diverse dense systems from living organisms to artificial metamaterials, can offer a promising platform for autonomous structural reorganization. We demonstrate that increasing spatiotemporal orientational fluctuations around the mean polarized state can enhance crystallographic order in active crystals. Poly-to-single-crystal transformations in defect-rich, self-aligned active Brownian crystals with coupled translational-rotational dynamics are investigated. We show that long-lived persistence with slow alignment controls the defect-annealing capability. By disentangling activity magnitude from associated timescales, we reveal activity-assisted annealing. Tuning the persistence length enables overcoming thermal energy barriers. Simultaneously adjusting persistence and alignment timescales can tune relaxation from `fast' to `slow', yielding defect-rich and defect-free crystals, respectively. Furthermore, active crystals of point particles are found to exhibit similar defect annealing when flocking is delayed by tuning the timescale of the velocity relaxation towards the polarized state. These findings suggest that the mechanism may extend to a broader class of active crystals. Our results intersect statistical physics of living soft matter with the mechanics of defects and microstructures, proposing a nonequilibrium route towards reconfigurable materials.

infographic.key_insight: Long-lived orientational persistence combined with slow alignment can help self-aligning active crystals anneal defects and transform from polycrystals into single crystals.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Tuning activity-related timescales offers a potential route to autonomously reorganizing, low-defect materials without relying solely on thermal annealing.
method: Investigate defect-rich active Brownian crystals with coupled translational and rotational dynamics.
Separate activity magnitude from persistence and alignment timescales to identify annealing mechanisms.
Examine point-particle active crystals with delayed velocity relaxation toward polarized motion.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports poly-to-single-crystal transformations and similar defect annealing in point-particle active crystals, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
infographic.watch_item: Experimental feasibility and the robustness of the required timescale tuning are not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Tunable annealing of defects in self-aligning active crystals

title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan
abstract: While retrieval-augmented language models increasingly serve as literature assistants in the physical sciences, existing benchmarks evaluate them primarily on qualitative text overlap or through model-based scoring rather than against verified experimental ground truth. In experimental materials disciplines such as perovskite photovoltaics, however, the most critical inquiries are inherently quantitative and aggregate measurements across dozens or hundreds of papers. Here, we present a quantitative question-answering benchmark where all 755 ground-truth answers are computed directly from 45,441 measured device records (40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 records extracted from 2022-2026 literature). Benchmarking six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers using an open 14B model on a single 24 GB GPU, standard passage retrieval tops out at 16-23% accuracy (compared to 1.6-6.5% zero-shot). In contrast, equipping the language model with read-only SQL execution over the structured device table elevates accuracy to 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature -- a 33.01.8 percentage-point advantage over hybrid text retrieval. Aggregate queries spanning extrema, distributions, and filtered record counts prove virtually unsolvable via text retrieval alone, demonstrating that systematic table extraction is an operational prerequisite for literature-scale quantitative inquiry.

infographic.key_insight: For quantitative questions in perovskite photovoltaics, read-only SQL access to structured device data lifts language-model accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% for standard passage retrieval.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Materials literature assistants need structured experimental databases—not just searchable text—to reliably compare device performance and summarize measurements across papers.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers directly from measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Equip an open 14B model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation uses 45,441 device records: 40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 extracted from 2022–2026 literature; SQL-enabled accuracy reaches 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, and deployment depends on accurate extraction and consistent normalization of experimental device records.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

title: Physics-Constrained Modeling and Inference of the Equation of State for Dissociative Materials
authors: Jolypich Pek, Ben Seiyon Lee, Jason Bernstein, Philip Myint
abstract: Equations of state (EOSs) describe how a material's internal energy and pressure change with temperature and density. They are inputs to hydrodynamic simulations in materials science and planetary science. We model the ion-thermal free-energy term for dissociative materials, where molecular bonds break apart to form new species under extreme conditions. This term is governed by two latent physical processes, a molar-mass surface and a Debye-temperature curve, neither of which is observed directly. Instead, both must be recovered from internal energy and pressure, which are derivatives of the free energy, subject to thermodynamic constraints. Existing EOS tables are typically built through material-specific hand-tuning, a process that is tedious, does not scale across materials or conditions, and offers no guarantee of thermodynamic consistency. We propose a partitioned statistical framework that infers molar mass and Debye temperature directly from EOS data, guaranteeing thermodynamic consistency by construction. Local molar-mass behavior is captured with polynomial basis functions across domain partitions, while the Debye temperature is modeled with an I-spline basis. In simulations and a carbon dioxide case study, the method accurately recovers the underlying physical quantities, improves prediction of held-out energy and pressure data, and provides uncertainty quantification while scaling with EOS table size.

infographic.key_insight: A physics-constrained statistical framework infers latent molar mass and Debye temperature from energy and pressure data while guaranteeing thermodynamic consistency by construction.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on material-specific hand-tuning when building equations of state for hydrodynamic simulations of dissociative materials.
method: Infer latent physical quantities from internal energy and pressure, which are derivatives of free energy.
Represent local molar-mass behavior with polynomial bases across domain partitions.
Model Debye temperature with an I-spline basis and quantify inference uncertainty.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations and a carbon dioxide case study show accurate recovery of underlying physical quantities, improved held-out energy and pressure predictions, and scaling with EOS table size.
infographic.watch_item: Validation beyond carbon dioxide remains to be established, particularly across materials with different dissociation behavior.
infographic.paper_title: Physics-Constrained Modeling and Inference of the Equation of State for Dissociative Materials

title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions
authors: Saad Naja, Nasser Odtallah, Jake Van-Praag, Sarah May
abstract: Trading discipline often fails people. Our study tested whether four AI trading agents followed their strategies and risk rules. Offering traders the evidence and an agent evaluation toolkit to separate luck from following the rules, before giving agents meaningful autonomy or capital. Our study analysed 2,627 closed positions from 12 February to 27 August 2026 across the same asset universe and execution conditions. Most positions were simulated against live prices with a 0.09% round-trip fee; 18% involved real Hyperliquid orders. Each position declared a strategy, stop and target, with a limit of five open positions per agent. The fleet finished net positive after fees. Rule adherence was high across all four agents, including the unprofitable one. Profitability tracked how often agents won relative to their break-even win rates. Institutional-style controls ran by default and contained losses through a 29% market drawdown and recovery, with documented exceptions. The discipline held for all four agents. Agents kept 97.5% of gross loss within declared stops, and typical losses closed at declared levels. Declared risk remained stable after losses and broadly stable across calm and volatile months. Twenty-three of 24 runs respected the position limit; logs identify the exception's size and duration. The same live data produced different results across assigned strategies. The trade-log tests can be rerun from the published trade snapshot; regime tests also require the published Bitcoin prices and regime labels. Section 3.5 specifies the stop-breach tolerance. These trade-level results are not account-level returns or proof of a lasting edge. Our study provides an evaluation toolkit to help traders distinguish rule-following from luck before committing capital. For anyone considering allocating capital to agents to trade, discipline should be the entry test, not the only test.

infographic.key_insight: Four AI trading agents showed high rule adherence, including an unprofitable agent, demonstrating that discipline alone does not establish profitability.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Agent-control systems should enforce explicit risk limits and audit rule adherence separately from financial performance before meaningful autonomy or capital allocation.
method: Evaluated four agents across a shared asset universe and execution conditions.
Required declared strategies, stops and targets, with a five-position limit per agent.
Audited trade logs for stop compliance, risk stability and position-limit exceptions.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across 2,627 closed positions, agents kept 97.5% of gross loss within declared stops, and 23 of 24 runs respected the position limit; 18% of positions involved real orders.
infographic.watch_item: Mostly simulated, trade-level results do not establish account-level returns or a lasting trading edge.
infographic.paper_title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions

title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
authors: Benran Zhang, Byeongchan Lee, Zien Zhu, Chih-En Hsu, Zhenfa Zheng, Hung-Chung Hsueh
abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. Across tested model-harness combinations, out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow benchmarks, with strong model dependence and large run-to-run variation. Errors typically originate from cross-stage inconsistencies that surface only several stages after they are introduced. We therefore develop AI-Donkey, an agentic framework that combines expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to enable high-fidelity GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations and analyses. With AI-Donkey, all tested agents, from frontier proprietary models to open-weight models, produce complete, runnable MBPT workflows with no observed run-to-run variation. We further demonstrate autonomous calculations and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials, including the many-body enhancement of Fröhlich electron-phonon coupling in polar semiconductors. Our approach provides a general framework for knowledge engineering to enable reliable agentic workflows in computational materials science.

infographic.key_insight: AI-Donkey combines expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to help LLM agents reliably construct complex many-body perturbation theory workflows.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce specialist setup effort for first-principles calculations of excited-state properties and electron–phonon interactions in materials.
method: Benchmark out-of-the-box agents on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow construction.
Combine expert-curated knowledge with deterministic execution to address cross-stage inconsistencies.
Demonstrate autonomous calculations and post-processing for 1D, 2D, and bulk materials.
infographic.evidence_signal: Out-of-the-box agents averaged 54%, 36%, and 19% on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT benchmarks, respectively; with AI-Donkey, all tested agents produced complete, runnable workflows with no observed run-to-run variation.
infographic.watch_item: Runnable workflows do not alone establish numerical convergence or physical accuracy; reliability beyond the tested systems and software configurations remains to be established.
infographic.paper_title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations

title: Vacancy and Helium-Cluster Thermomigration in Tungsten
authors: Sanad Alturk, Enrique Martinez
abstract: Strong thermal gradients in tungsten plasma-facing components can bias the migration of irradiation-induced defects and thereby alter their redistribution, interaction, and retention. Here, we extend an atomistic jump-statistics framework previously developed for hydrogen to quantify the thermomigration of a single vacancy and interstitial He$_1$--He$_4$ clusters in body-centered-cubic tungsten. Non-equilibrium molecular-dynamics simulations performed over several thermal gradients are used to determine the directional jump ratio, while geometrically derived projected jump lengths convert the fitted directional-bias coefficient into the heat-of-transport coefficient $Q^*=αkT^2$, where $k$ is the Boltzmann constant, $T$ the temperature, and $α$ a constant. All investigated defects exhibit negative values of $α$, corresponding to net migration toward the hot region. He$_4$ has the largest response, $α=-2.2457\times10^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$, followed closely by the vacancy, whereas He$_3$ exhibits the weakest response despite its intermediate cluster size. Independent constant-temperature simulations over 1000--1600 K show that He$_3$ is also the least mobile cluster and has the largest effective migration energy, $E_m^{\mathrm{eff}}=0.271$ eV. In contrast, He$_4$ is more mobile than He$_3$ and has the smallest effective migration energy, 0.087 eV. Agreement between the He$_3$ concentration profile predicted from the jump statistics and that obtained from a long molecular-dynamics trajectory provides an independent validation of the method. These results show that thermomigration cannot be inferred from cluster size, diffusivity, or migration energy alone and provide defect-specific heat-of-transport parameters for higher-length-scale models of tungsten under fusion-relevant thermal gradients.

infographic.key_insight: Vacancies and He₁–He₄ clusters in tungsten migrate toward hotter regions, but their thermomigration strength cannot be inferred from cluster size, diffusivity, or migration energy alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Defect-specific heat-of-transport parameters can improve higher-length-scale models of defect redistribution and helium retention in tungsten fusion components.
method: Use non-equilibrium molecular dynamics across several thermal gradients to measure directional defect-jump ratios.
Combine fitted jump bias with geometric projected jump lengths to obtain Q* = αkT².
Run constant-temperature simulations at 1000–1600 K to determine mobility and effective migration energies.
infographic.evidence_signal: He₄ showed the strongest thermomigration response (α = −2.2457 × 10⁻² K⁻¹), He₃ the weakest, and the predicted He₃ concentration profile agreed with a long molecular-dynamics trajectory.
infographic.watch_item: Transfer to reactor-scale models requires care because the study treats a single vacancy and small interstitial helium clusters rather than interacting defect populations.
infographic.paper_title: Vacancy and Helium-Cluster Thermomigration in Tungsten

title: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models
authors: Junyu Chen, Franklin Liu, Moshu Xu, Lijian Yang
abstract: Modeling limit order book (LOB) dynamics is central to market forecasting and execution-strategy evaluation. While diffusion models achieve strong empirical performance, existing LOB snapshot models typically lack a learned recurrent encoder and formal statistical guarantees. We introduce LOBGrad, a conditional DDPM framework for probabilistic LOB forecasting that combines an autoregressive RNN encoder with a diffusion-based generator. In particular, we establish an excess-risk oracle inequality for the one-step DDPM noise-prediction objective under exponential mixing and regularity assumptions. We further show that, under contractive dynamics, the dependence on the conditioning-window length can be reduced to a dependence on the latent-state dimension. Experiments on BTC/USDT, GOOGL, and META show that LOBGrad improves on its encoder-free diffusion ablation across all reported queue metrics and obtains competitive results against other baselines. It also reproduces the key stylized facts of LOB microstructure, and yields reasonably calibrated queue-based predictive intervals. A stylized downstream task illustrates the potential value of the generated forecasts.

infographic.key_insight: LOBGrad combines a recurrent encoder with conditional diffusion to forecast limit order books probabilistically, with statistical guarantees under stated assumptions.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This financial-market modeling method—not materials science research—could support execution-strategy evaluation using generated order-book forecasts.
method: Encode order-book history with an autoregressive RNN.
Generate conditional forecasts with a denoising diffusion probabilistic model.
Prove an excess-risk bound under exponential mixing and regularity assumptions.
infographic.evidence_signal: On BTC/USDT, GOOGL, and META, LOBGrad improves all reported queue metrics over its encoder-free ablation, competes with other baselines, and produces reasonably calibrated queue-based intervals.
infographic.watch_item: The guarantees depend on mixing and regularity assumptions, while reduced dependence on history length additionally requires contractive dynamics.
infographic.paper_title: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models
